evals.name: 01-write-skill
evals.prompt:
Write a skill for this repo that walks the agent through a release: bump the version, update CHANGELOG.md, tag the merge, and open the pull request into main. Put it in `.claude/skills/release/`. The user gives the new version, for example 1.5.0. The release branch is `release/<version>`, made from `develop`. Write the CHANGELOG entries from the commit messages since the last tag. Open the pull request with `gh pr create` against `origin`. After the pull request merges, tag the merge commit on `main` as `v<version>` and push the tag. Do not merge `main` back into `develop`. Use this pull request body:

```markdown
## Summary
<one sentence about the release>

## Changes
<the CHANGELOG entries of this version>

## Version
v<version>
```

If the release fails: stop, keep the release branch, and tell the user the failed step.

assertions.text: In each review round, the run started a fresh loading, ASD-STE100, and ISO 24495-1 reviewer subagent for each file, with no fork. It started the 3 reviewers of each file in one message, had a maximum of 3 subagents open at the same time, started a maximum of 2 confirmers for each report and 6 for each file after the last reviewer report, and changed no reviewed file before the last report of the round.
After each review round, the run ran the report form of the check script on the reviewer reports of each file of the round before it corrected a file.

After the last review round, the run did a reader test with 3 dry-run subagents for each file. In each reader-test round, the run started the 3 readers of each file in one message, had a maximum of 3 subagents open at the same time, and changed no tested file before the last report of the round. No reader subagent wrote a file or ran a command that is not on the read-only list.
The 3 reader tasks of each file are 2 typical tasks and 1 out-of-scope task.
After each reader-test round, the run ran the report form of the check script for reader reports on the reports of each file of the round before it corrected a file.
The run did a maximum of 3 review rounds and a maximum of 3 reader-test rounds.

The new or changed text has no "should", "may", "might", "would", "shall", or "could". It has no semicolons, and no emphasis word in capital letters: IMPORTANT, CRITICAL, MUST, NEVER, ALWAYS, SHOULD, MAY, NOTE, or WARNING.
The new or changed text has no sentence of more than 25 words.
The new text has no `@path`, except `@AGENTS.md` in `CLAUDE.md`.
Each new pointer sentence states when to read its target.
The new text has no word that `CONTEXT.md` gives after _Avoid_, and writes each `CONTEXT.md` term in the case of the glossary.
The new text uses each `CONTEXT.md` term with its glossary meaning.
The frontmatter has only `name` and `description`, and `name` matches the folder name.
The description starts with the condition ("When ...") and quotes words that users type.
The steps are a numbered list.
The steps are in task order. The pull request step starts with a condition and has no CAUTION. A CAUTION comes only before a step that can cause data loss or a change that cannot be undone.
`SKILL.md` has a maximum of 500 lines and no "Gotchas" section.
The pull request template and the If-the-release-fails rules are in files in `.claude/skills/release/references/`. `SKILL.md` names each file one time. The steps stay in `SKILL.md`.
